Blade-to-coolant convection heat-transfer coefficients were obtained over a range of turbine speeds from 2000 to 14,500 rpm and inlet-gas temperatures from 400°F to 1300°F.
Coolant flow rates from 0.7 to 7 gallons per minute, equivalent to mass velocities of 1565 to 15,650 lb/min/ft^2, were investigated.
Accounting for radial conduction from the blade to the disk rim reduced the calculated Nusselt numbers by 14-31% compared to neglecting conduction.
Natural convection had a negligible effect on blade-to-coolant heat transfer over the Grashof number range of 3x10^9 to 4x10^12.
The turbine data agreed closely with the correlation for laminar flow of heated liquids through stationary tubes, with a maximum deviation of 17% for Graetz numbers from 600 to 2400.
The range of Graetz numbers investigated was from 230 to 2400.
The characteristic dimension used in the Nusselt and Graetz numbers was the length of the radial coolant passage in the blade.
The Nusselt number increased with increasing Graetz number in the natural convection correlation, indicating that coolant flow rate, not speed, governed the heat transfer.
The researchers hypothesized that the combination of forced and natural convection flows in the coolant passages may have led to a net negligible effect on the average heat transfer coefficient.

Using stationary-tube blade-to-coolant coefficients and theoretical gas-to-blade coefficients, the maximum deviation of calculated average midspan blade temperatures from experimental data was 190°F at 1650°F.
The turbine had 50 impulse blades of constant cross section and no twist, with a tip diameter of 12.06 inches, chord of 0.744 inch, and span of 1.15 inches.
Coolant passages near the leading and trailing edges had a diameter of 0.062 inches, while passages near the blade center had a diameter of 0.099 inches.
The crossover passage near the blade tip connecting the radial coolant passages had a diameter of 0.062 inches.
Blade temperatures were measured using a rotating thermocouple pick-up system with six thermocouples located at various positions on the blades.
The total heat transferred to the coolant was determined from the coolant weight flow and temperature rise.
